correctness.rationale: For a monotone self-map \(f\) of a finite poset, \(x\le f(x)\) or \(f(x)\le x\) yields a monotone iterate chain that stabilizes at a fixed point. Hence a fixed-point-free map under incomparability degree at most one must send each point to its unique incomparable mate. This forces a unique involution \(\tau\). If two mate pairs are distinct, monotonicity of \(\tau\) and transitivity force all four cross-comparisons to have the same direction, so the pairs form a total order and the poset is an ordinal sum of two-point antichains. Conversely the levelwise swap is isotone and fixed-point-free. The order complex is the join of \(k\) copies of \(S^0\), hence \(S^{k-1}\); the swap is antipodal and has degree \((-1)^k\). The finite verifier only corroborates low orders and is not used for the universal proof.
residual_risks: The theorem is elementary enough that an older poset fixed-point note may contain an equivalent formulation under different terminology.
